newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal inflation to continue slowing -INE.
newsitem.headline: Portugal inflation to continue slowing -INE.

text.p: The trend towards slower inflation in Portugal during 1997 should not been broken by the rise in the year-on-year rate registered in May, the National Statistics Institute said.
The consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.1 percent in May after 1.8 percent rise in April.

"The 2.1 percent year-on-year rise in the CPI in May, reversed the downward trend of previous months. Neverthless, the underlying trend continues to point to a slowing in," INE said in its monthly economic report.
Despite the rise in the year-on-year rate last month, the 12-month rolling average rate, the government's benchmark, eased to 3.0 percent from 3.1 percent in April.
INE noted that the index of tradable goods, excluding food, showed that price rises slowed to 1.6 percent from 1.7 percent in May.
The Institute said that the reversal of the trend in May was due to unusual behaviour of a few food products -- pork and potatoes -- together with the rise in tobacco prices.
It noted that the indicators for the growth in private consumption had also continued to slow in May.
Wages rose 3.4 percent year-on-year in the three months to end-April, it said. INE gave no comparison.
